headline.title: First flakes for Northern Vermont.
headline.text: Up to {{s:2.5}} on the summit of Jay Peak Friday morning to early Saturday. All 19 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Quiet before the storm today, and then rain and gusty winds tomorrow.
Cool, breezy weather with some mountain snow on Saturday will turn drier for the new week.
The long term continues to be very quiet with temperatures at or above normal and high confidence of an extended dry period of weather likely.

ALY.excerpt:
) A strong cold front will bring gusty winds, showers, and a few thunderstorms to the region for Friday. Continued gusty and unseasonably chilly conditions are expected Friday night into Saturday. A coating of snow is possible in the high terrain Friday night.
) Dry weather with temperatures moderating to near seasonable levels Sunday into early next week.

GYX.excerpt:
Low pressure crosses on Friday, bringing beneficial rainfall to the area.
A seasonably cold airmass pushes in behind the system to start the weekend, with wintry conditions across the higher terrain.
Mild and dry conditions look to persist from Sunday through much of next week as high pressure dominates over the Northeast.

BUF.excerpt:
) Periods of rain tonight through Friday, along with gusty winds.
) Much colder Friday night through Saturday night with a few wet snowflakes possible early Saturday morning.

PHI.excerpt:
A warm front will move north through the region tonight, followed by a strong cold front that will pose the threat of severe weather on Friday afternoon and evening.
Widespread frost and freeze conditions are increasingly likely Saturday night.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Just a coating for the high peaks.
paras: Light snow Friday morning to early Saturday: Jay Peak {{s:1.8}}, Smugglers' Notch {{s:1.2}}, Bolton Valley {{s:0.8}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0.3,4.6}} at Jay Peak. Rain mixes in even up high at times.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:28}} to {{t:57}}, with up to {{s:1.4}} of snow and gusts near {{w:42}} up top.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 26).
NWS Burlington forecasters: "Quiet before the storm today, and then rain and gusty winds tomorrow."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.

insights.text: First flakes: about {{s:1.8}} at the summit Friday morning to early Saturday (models {{r:0.3,4.6}}). It starts as rain ({{l:1.36}}), even at the summit, then changes to snow Friday night as colder air arrives. It won't last: highs reach {{t:50}} Monday.
Cold enough to make snow Saturday morning to Sunday morning: about 26 hours at or below {{t:26}} at mid-mountain, counting humidity. Whether the guns run is up to the resort.
Typically opens around Nov 27, 43 days out.
